_about: Where the breadboard's holes are in the eye's frame, so a wiring state can be drawn on a photograph (tools/board-overlay.py).

MEASURED 2026-09-13 off the 15:40 baseline board frame (eye.py grab b0-all, focus 20, zoom 100), by reading the printed column numbers and the hole rows under pixel rulers: a column's y is quadratic in its number (the camera looks along the board at an angle, so the pitch grows from about 17.6 px at column 35 to 21 px at column 1); a hole row's x drifts linearly with y between the top and bottom readings.
A map is for one camera pose. The frame it was read from is named; a frame from another pose needs its own reading.
chips: as built, read off the eye (docs/as-built-v1b.md, the QA note): pin 1 at the high-column end, pins 1 to n/2 down the side toward the middle board, n/2+1 to n up the side toward the rails.

RIG, SECOND POSE 2026-09-15 off b10-all.jpg: the boards shifted right under the fixed camera and the UNO's leads re-run direct. The map is read automatically now: every hole centre in the frame by normalised correlation with a hole template (1201 found), the hole rows as five evenly spaced rows fitted to the centres' y (a to e at [396, 419, 442, 465, 488], f to j at [545, 568, 591, 614, 637], pitch 23.0 px; the rails' hole rows at [300, 324]), the columns walked leftward from the board's last hole (column 1) through the x peaks of the a-to-e and f-to-j bands with an adaptive pitch, a missing peak (under a wire) interpolated; the pitch shrinks from about 24.5 px at column 1 to 23.5 at column 50 (the lens), so the anchors are the walked positions every fifth column and the map interpolates between them. frame_rotate keeps the map's convention: map x = 1080 - camera y, map y = camera x.
